conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence is an institutional assurance and access-governance failure surface rather than evidence of model misconduct. Independent frontier-model evaluation depends on evaluators receiving timely access before deployment or restricted release. Where an external national safety institute that previously evaluated a provider's frontier models no longer receives pre-release access, the state's ability to independently characterize capability, validate safeguards and identify weaknesses before use is reduced. The governance issue is therefore the interruption of an established assurance pathway and the dependence of national safety oversight on provider-controlled and potentially geopolitically constrained model access. Loss of voluntary evaluator access retains ambiguous investigative-authority and oversight boundaries. It establishes neither a compulsory production duty nor institutional capture, unsafe deployment or absence of every independent evaluation.
